scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning:
Okay, let's tackle this scenario. The user is asking if they're the asshole (AITA) for selling their former roommate's video games. The roommate left without taking his stuff, and after multiple attempts to get him to pick it up, the user sold the games for $600. Now the roommate is upset and wants his money back.

First, I need to consider the moral aspects here. The roommate didn't take his belongings, which is his responsibility. The user tried to communicate for two weeks, which shows effort. The landlord's policy might have made it costly for the roommate to leave things, but he didn't act. By selling the games, the user is disposing of the items as per the situation. Legally, there's nothing owed, but morally, is it right to sell someone else's property without their consent?

Even though the roommate didn't take his stuff, selling it could be seen as taking advantage of the situation. The user might argue that the roommate had the chance to retrieve his items but didn't. However, the roommate's belongings are his, and selling them without permission could be considered unethical. The user didn't ask for permission, which is a key point. Even if the roommate was negligent, the user's action might still be morally questionable because they didn't seek consent. 

The roommate's reaction is understandable because his games were sold without his knowledge. The user's intention was to get rid of the items, but the method might not be justified. The moral acceptability here hinges on whether the user had the right to sell the items without the owner's approval. Since the roommate didn't take his things, maybe the user had a duty to dispose of them, but selling for profit could be seen as exploiting the situation. 

In many ethical frameworks, taking someone else's property without consent is wrong, even if the owner was negligent. The user should have either given the items to the landlord or disposed of them properly without selling. Selling for profit might be seen as morally unacceptable because it's using the roommate's property for personal gain without his consent. Therefore, the action is likely morally unacceptable.
